title: Audit exporter service scaffold + config sync (polling/streaming), tenant isolation, and baseline health endpoints
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Stand up the initial audit-log-exporter service used by the SIEM-ready audit export beta. This issue covers (1) service scaffolding that can run in hosted + dedicated environments, (2) config synchronization from the control plane (polling now; optional streaming path), (3) per-tenant isolation boundaries in the exporter runtime, and (4) baseline health endpoints to support SRE readiness and Console status surfaces.

Context
We are building an exporter that delivers canonical audit events to customer destinations (Splunk HEC / Datadog Logs / S3) with at-least-once delivery. The exporter must be safe in a multi-tenant environment: configs, event routing, and checkpoints must never cross tenant boundaries. We also need operationally friendly primitives early: health/readiness endpoints, structured logs, and a stable config sync contract.

Scope
1) Service scaffolding
- New service repo/module: audit-log-exporter.
- Standard Redwood service layout (config, DI wiring, logging, metrics hooks, deploy manifests stubs).
- Local dev harness that can run the exporter with a fake control-plane config endpoint and synthetic audit event feed.

2) Config sync from control plane
- Config fetch client with tenant scoping.
- Polling loop with jittered interval and exponential backoff on failures.
- Config versioning: exporter caches last-applied config by (tenant_id, export_config_id, config_version) and only rehydrates pipelines when version changes.
- Safe defaults:
  - If config cannot be fetched at startup, exporter comes up in a non-exporting state but stays healthy (readyz fails until at least one successful config fetch OR an explicit "no eligible tenants" state is confirmed; see below).
  - If a previously valid config becomes invalid/unparseable (unexpected schema), exporter keeps last-known-good config and emits a high-severity log + metric (follow-up alerting in ENG-5168).
- Streaming hook (optional path): keep a placeholder interface for "ConfigSource" that can be implemented via SSE/gRPC push later. For beta we are polling-first to reduce coupling and operational risk.

3) Per-tenant isolation model
- Exporter runtime maintains isolated execution contexts per tenant:
  - TenantContext: {tenant_id, configs[], destination clients, checkpoint store handle, rate limits}.
  - No shared mutable state across tenants other than bounded shared worker threads.
- Each tenant has its own:
  - adapter instances (or adapter client pools keyed by tenant_id + destination_id)
  - retry state/circuit breakers
  - checkpoint namespace/prefix
- Guardrails:
  - All processing functions take tenant_id as an explicit parameter and validate it matches the context.
  - Logs include tenant_id and export_config_id for all export actions; never log destination secrets.
  - Metric label cardinality is bounded (tenant_id is not used as a label in Prometheus metrics by default; we use hashed/enum labels like destination_type, result, error_class; tenant-level drilldown is via logs/traces and internal admin tooling).

4) Baseline health endpoints
- /healthz: process liveness (always 200 once server is up).
- /readyz: readiness for exporting:
  - 200 when config sync has succeeded at least once OR when feature flag indicates exporter is disabled for this environment (so we don’t block deploys in non-beta clusters).
  - 503 when exporter is expected to run but cannot reach control plane for initial sync.
- /debug/config (admin-only, behind internal auth): returns redacted view of applied config versions per tenant (no secrets; destination URLs are normalized/redacted). This endpoint is meant for internal debugging only during beta.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for this ticket)
- Delivery semantics, checkpointing, and adapter logic (tracked in ENG-5144 / ENG-5151 / ENG-5156 and ADR on delivery semantics).
- Filtering engine implementation (ENG-5160).
- Full observability dashboards/alerts (ENG-5168).
- DLQ and replay tooling (ENG-5164).

Design notes / decisions
- Polling cadence (beta default): 30s with jitter; backoff max 5m. Rationale: config changes are relatively infrequent in beta; polling avoids coupling exporter availability to long-lived streams.
- Config invalidation: on delete/disable, exporter must tear down the corresponding pipeline and stop exporting for that config. We retain checkpoints in storage for N days (policy to be defined in retention/export responsibilities doc) to allow re-enable without forced backfill.
- Tenant allowlist gating: exporter only instantiates TenantContexts for tenants returned by the control plane as enabled for SIEM export beta (feature-flag/allowlist enforced server-side in control plane; exporter treats it as authoritative).

Acceptance criteria
- A new audit-log-exporter service exists with:
  - runnable binary/container in dev
  - standard logging and configuration
  - health endpoints wired
- Exporter can successfully fetch export configs from the control plane API (feature-flagged) and keep them up to date via polling.
- Config changes are applied without restart:
  - create/update/delete reflected within one poll interval
  - exporter does not crash on transient control-plane errors
- Demonstrated tenant isolation:
  - unit/integration test that two tenants with different destinations do not cross-write
  - checkpoint namespace includes tenant_id and export_config_id
- Ready/readiness behavior documented for SRE + deploy owners.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - config parsing/validation failures (ensure last-known-good behavior)
  - polling/backoff behavior
  - tenant context mapping correctness
- Integration tests (local harness):
  - fake control plane returns changing configs over time
  - exporter logs applied versions and updates
- Manual test:
  - run exporter locally, point to staging control plane, enable a test tenant via allowlist, verify /readyz flips to 200 after first sync.

Rollout / operational notes
- Service is safe to deploy disabled-by-default (feature flag off / no tenants returned).
- SRE should not page on initial rollout for "no eligible tenants"; readiness should not flap in non-beta clusters.
- Any config sync errors should be visible in logs; metrics/alerts will be added in ENG-5168.

Links
- GitHub PR: sources/github/audit-log-exporter/pr-1042-bootstrap-audit-exporter-service-and-ci.json
- GitHub PR: sources/github/audit-log-exporter/pr-1049-add-config-sync-from-control-plane.json
- Dependency: sources/github/redwood/pr-28766-control-plane-export-config-api-endpoints.json (ENG-5132)
- Related runbook (future): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-audit-exporter-delivery-failures.json

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want to support a lightweight push channel (SSE) for config changes during GA to reduce propagation delay? (Not needed for beta; revisit after we have real-world config churn data.)
- Confirm readiness semantics with SRE: when control plane is down, do we prefer readyz fail (remove from service) or stay ready but stop exporting? Current proposal: if we already have an applied config, stay ready and continue exporting based on last-known-good until max staleness threshold (to be added with backpressure/max-lag safety work).

Outcome
Implemented via PRs 1042 and 1049; exporter can boot, poll for configs with tenant scoping, and exposes /healthz and /readyz endpoints with beta-safe semantics. TenantContext boundaries are explicit and will be exercised further as adapters and checkpointing land.
comments: 2025-02-04 (Ethan Park): Priority is P0 because everything else (adapters, filtering, SLOs) depends on having a stable service + config sync. Please keep the config source interface pluggable so we can consider push later.
2025-02-07 (Diego Santos): Scaffold is up with CI + basic HTTP server. Added /healthz and /readyz stubs; next is wiring config polling client and applying to an in-memory registry keyed by tenant_id.

2025-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Please ensure no secrets end up in logs or debug endpoints. For /debug/config, require internal auth and return only redacted destinations (no tokens, no full headers). Also confirm tenant_id is always passed explicitly through processing path (avoid implicit globals).

2025-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Control plane endpoint shape is stable enough for polling. We’ll return only allowlisted tenants while feature flag is on; exporter should treat empty list as normal/ready when running in non-beta clusters.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Readiness semantics: agree that lack of initial sync should make /readyz 503 in beta-enabled clusters. Once synced at least once, remain ready even if control plane has an outage; alerting should be on export lag/error, not config sync transient failures.

2025-02-18 (Diego Santos): Config polling + backoff in place. Implemented last-known-good behavior on parse errors and explicit tenant-scoped registries. Added a small local harness to simulate config changes every N seconds.
2025-02-21 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-5168 for metrics and ENG-5164 for DLQ/replay. Please keep an eye on any accidental tenant_id label use as we add Prom metrics.
